title: Today’s Research Reports on Stocks to Watch: IBM and Apple
text: https://rdinvesting.com/news/?ticker=AAPL International Business Machines Corporation shares were down 7.63% on nearly 19.5 million shares traded on Wednesday. It was disappointing financial results this week that sent shares of IBM lower yesterday. Senior VP and CFO said on the earnings call, "In the third quarter, we delivered $18.8 billion of revenue, $3.6 billion of operating pretax income and $3.42 of operating earnings per share, and over the last 12 months, we generated $12.2 billion of free cash flow with realization over 100%. As compared to last year, our revenue was flat at constant currency, though down 2% with the impact of the stronger dollar. Gross profit margin was flat, which is the best year-to-year performance in years. The improvement was led by services margin expansion. We expanded our overall operating pretax margin, and we grew operating profit and earnings per share." Earnings of $3.42 per share were two cents higher than what analysts expected. Revenue at $18.76 billion was lower than the $19.10 billion as expected by analysts. "IBM still has a revenue growth problem," Stifel analysts wrote in a Tuesday note. Access RDI’s International Business Machines Corporation Research Report at: https://rdinvesting.com/news/?ticker=IBM Apple Inc. shares closed down modestly 0.43% on Wednesday on about 20 million shares traded. The tech giant has launched a website that is devoted to privacy. It gives the option for anyone to see all of the information that their iPhones, iPads and Macs have collected about them and sent to Apple. EU customers have already been able to use the site since May, when the new EU-wide data protection rules, known as General Data Protection Regulation, or GDPR, went into effect. Certain mandated companies that operate in Europe allow customers to obtain a copy of their own data. Apple is now allowing users in the United States, Canada, Australia and New Zealand see and download all information that it has collected on them. It also gives users a simpler way to make changes to the data, suspend their Apple account or even permanently delete it. Access RDI’s Apple Inc.
